key_insight: Two deep neural networks enable inverse design of superconducting RF cavities and transmon qubits by mapping target electromagnetic and coupling properties directly to candidate geometries.
engineering_relevance: This approach can substantially speed up quantum hardware design by reducing reliance on costly iterative simulation when tuning bosonic cavity-transmon systems.
method: DNN 1: propose SRF cavity geometries from target cavity observables.
DNN 2: propose transmon designs from target qubit-cavity targets (g, νq, α).
Use end-to-end re-simulation to validate whether recovered designs meet the requested specifications.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that candidate designs matched targets to within about 5% for cavities and about 2% for transmons after re-simulation.
watch_item: Inverse design remains one-to-many, so multiple valid geometries may exist and practical fabrication tolerances could shift the realized couplings.
paper_title: Neural-Network Inverse Design of SRF Cavities and Transmons for Bosonic Quantum Computation
